requirements.statement: The aircraft shall translate crew intent into controlled aircraft motion.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate traceability from crew commands through propulsion and control-surface functions to aircraft motion.

requirements.statement: The propulsion system shall provide thrust in response to aircraft control demands.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Show a complete command, electrical-power, and thrust path for each propulsion channel.

requirements.statement: The electrical power system shall supply the essential DC loads required for controlled flight.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Review every essential load against its allocated supply, interfaces, and failure response.

requirements.statement: The left motor shall convert supplied phase power into commanded shaft torque.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate the phase-power input, torque output, and associated failure-mode coverage for the installed left motor.

requirements.statement: The hydraulic controller power connector shall deliver protected 28 V DC power without an interruption longer than 20 ms.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: No interruption longer than 20 ms and contact resistance below 20 mΩ during the defined qualification exposure.
requirements.source: Illustrative aircraft hydraulic controller design target
requirements.verification_method: Continuity monitoring during vibration and thermal testing

requirements.statement: The hydraulic pressure sensor shall report delivery manifold pressure within ±2% of full scale.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Absolute error does not exceed 2% of full scale over the defined calibration and temperature points.
requirements.source: Illustrative aircraft hydraulic controller design target

requirements.statement: The hydraulic controller shall maintain commanded hydraulic pressure during its 1,000-hour ground qualification exposure.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: No loss of commanded hydraulic pressure for more than 2 seconds; demonstrate R(1000 h) ≥ 0.99 at 90% confidence.
requirements.source: Illustrative aircraft hydraulic controller design target
requirements.verification_method: Reliability demonstration with an agreed exposure and failure definition

requirements.statement: The hydraulic controller shall issue a safe-state command and maintenance indication within 100 ms of a detectable power-path fault.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The safe-state command and maintenance indication occur within the illustrative 100 ms fault-tolerant interval.
requirements.source: Illustrative aircraft hydraulic controller design target
requirements.verification_method: Boundary fault injection with timestamped response capture

verification_cases.acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate traceability from crew commands through propulsion and control-surface functions to aircraft motion.
Show a complete command, electrical-power, and thrust path for each propulsion channel.
Review every essential load against its allocated supply, interfaces, and failure response.
Demonstrate the phase-power input, torque output, and associated failure-mode coverage for the installed left motor.

verification_cases.objective: Verify hydraulic controller power continuity through its qualification exposure.
verification_cases.acceptance_criteria: No interruption longer than 20 ms and contact resistance below 20 mΩ during the defined qualification exposure.

blocks.content: A fictional aircraft architecture organized from the L1 aircraft through L2 systems, L3 subsystems and L4 components. The canonical System Model supplies the shared hierarchy, resource functions and interfaces for FMEA, prediction, and linked hydraulic analysis examples. Aircraft architecture, numerical engineering inputs, ratings, test identifiers and evidence references are illustrative training material; the NIST statistical datasets retain their documented source attribution.

blocks.content: Architecture background: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, Chapter 7 — Aircraft Systems (https://www.faa.gov/regulationspolicies/handbooksmanuals/aviation/phak/chapter-7-aircraft-systems); NASA X-57 technical papers (https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/armd/x-57-technical-papers/). These sources inform the fictional example’s organization and system interfaces; they do not substantiate its illustrative reliability inputs.

planning.subject: Aircraft hydraulic controller and immediate electrical, pressure, and status interfaces
planning.scope: L3 Hydraulic Controller Assembly and its L4 power connector, pressure sensor, and voltage monitor; shared aircraft electrical supply, hydraulic pump commands, and crew status interfaces.
planning.exclusions: Complete aircraft safety assessment, flight certification, and unmodeled failure combinations.
planning.intent: Identify illustrative causes and effects of loss or degradation of commanded aircraft hydraulic pressure.
planning.tasks: Design review, analysis, verification, action closure
planning.tools: System requirements, hazard log, FRACAS, verification evidence
planning.assumptions: Illustrative training analysis of the aircraft hydraulic controller. Existing example ratings, test identifiers, and numerical assumptions are demonstration inputs, not substantiated aircraft safety or reliability evidence.
